memoryText: And they sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to the LORD, For he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever toward Israel.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Ezra 3:11 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This sentence was sung by a small group of people standing in front of a foundation. They had come back to a ruined city. The walls were down. The temple was a pile of stones. And they sang.

“They sang responsively.” One group sang a line, and another answered. Worship together has a shape: we speak to each other and to God. No one is alone. In a time of rebuilding, they needed each other’s voices.

“Praising and giving thanks to the LORD.” The foundation was only a foundation. But they praised God for what he had done, not for what was finished. Gratitude does not wait until the work is complete.

“For he is good.” This is the reason for praise: God himself, not their circumstances. The circumstances were mixed. The old men were weeping. Persia was still in charge. Enemies were waiting. But God was good.

“For his steadfast love endures forever toward Israel.” The word “endures” reminds us that the exile did not end it. Seventy years of captivity could not cancel God’s covenant love. It is the same refrain as Psalm 136 and the same truth as Lamentations 3. Their song was an act of faith: the God who sent them away has brought them back.

Say this verse whenever you stand at the foundation of something that is not yet finished. You do not have to wait for the walls to go up. Sing now.
weekInReview: This week you finished the Old Testament’s exile story and began its last chapter. You finished Daniel with the writing on the wall, the lions’ den, the vision of the Son of Man, and the promise of resurrection. Then, on the first day of Unit 14, you read the decree of Cyrus and followed the first returning exiles home. You saw them build the altar before the temple, and lay the foundation to the sound of trumpets, cymbals, and a song of thanks. And you heard the sound that mixes shouting with weeping. The week taught that God keeps his promises and moves the hearts of kings, that he brings his people home, and that the return, though real, is still only a beginning.
reflectionQuestions: The returning exiles built the altar before they built anything else. What would it look like to put worship first in your day, your work, or your home?
The old men wept when they saw the small foundation. Is there something in your life that is smaller than you hoped, and how might God want you to receive it?
God stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, a pagan king, to fulfill his word. Where have you seen God work through someone who did not know him?
prayerPrompts: Give thanks to God for his steadfast love.
Thank him for bringing his people home.
